Messages.Author: Damnans
Messages.Body:
Storyline - Ragnarök, the Final Battle

Synopsis

The All High, a legendary Gangrel elder, is missing. An army of monsters has descended from the mountains of Norway and Sweden intent on wreaking havoc upon the World, upsetting the ages-old conflict between sleeping Methuselahs.
Rules

Ragnarök, The Final Battle is a constructed V:TES Storyline event designed for the 2013 VTES European Championship.

Except as noted in these instructions, each Storyline game will follow the VEKN Constructed Tournament rules for card play and deck construction. Each Storyline game will be timed to a maximum duration of 2 hours.

At least 75% (e.g. 9 out of 12) of the vampires in the player's crypt must belong to the same clan. In addition to the standard list of VEKN banned cards, Recalled to the Founder (Event) is banned from play.

Any single V:TES game played with 4-5 players using Storyline legal decks between 00:00 Monday 30th September and 00:00 Thursday 31st October anywhere in the world that uses the described game modifications may contribute towards the Ragnarök Storyline and have its results submitted.

The pack provided in support of the Ragnarök Storyline includes several sheets of additional cards:
Adversary cards — monsters to fight during the game Reward cards — prizes to be won during the game An All-High vampire card Optional Brunhilde Advanced and Valkyrie vampire cards which may be used in any player's crypt An optional set of additional werewolf themed cards which may be used in any player's library  Before the game begins shuffle the Adversary cards and deal out 7 of each to form a deck, which is placed in the centre of the table. Do the same with the Reward cards. The 2 remaining cards from each set should be placed to one side without revealing them. Also place the All High vampire card in the centre of the table.

After each player has taken two turns the top card of each of the Adversary and Reward decks are revealed. Counters should be placed on the Adversary to represent its starting life. The text on the Adversary will take immediate effect.

Adversaries are immune to all card effects which target allies, and are also immune to all card effects which target minions controlled by other Methuselahs.

In each player's minion phase, any minion controlled by that player may take an undirected action to enter combat with the revealed Adversary. If its life is reduced to zero by combat damage it is burned and removed from the game.

The controller of acting minion that burned the Adversary takes the revealed Reward card and may place it on any minion he or she controls.

The next top card from each deck is then revealed. This sequence is repeated 7 times until there are no Adversary or Reward cards left on the table.

When the last Adversary is burned all players left in the game make an open bid for control of the All High using their pool, starting with the active player. The minimum bid is 1 pool. Players are not forced to bid if they do not wish to. The player that wins this bid moves the All High to his or her ready region with 0 blood, and play continues as normal. All of the pool bid by the winner is returned to the blood bank. The losers of the bid do not lose any pool.

An FAQ is included in the pack which should answer many common questions.

All players are recommended to download and print their own copies of the Storyline pack from the link below. Printed copies will be circulated at the EC but they will be limited in number - players are advised to bring their own copies if possible.

Mike Nudd, VEKN Storyline Coordinator

DOWNLOADS   Prologue   Rules   Crypt Cards   Library Cards   Adversary and Reward Cards

V:EKN Website Coordinator

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> AaronC wrote:
> So far it looks like an interesting storyline. However, I see a glaring problem with the adversaries: none of them has a manuever to go to close and none of them has a ranged attack.
>
Combine that with the fact that the enter combat action is innate and repeatable, and that the replacement Adversary turns up immediately, and a single Methuselah with a clutch of Freak Drives, guns, and Taste of Vitae (to pay for the Freaks) could take out pretty much all the Adversaries in one turn.

Additionally, if an Adversary is reduced to zero life outside combat, it appears from the FAQs that it does not burn. But then it has no method for gaining life, so a few Horseshoes could stall the whole game. (Horseshoe targets ready minions, unlike Cryptic Mission which would target an ally.) Skoll is an obvious exception. Note that "reduced to zero life in combat" is text that, by pre-existing rulings on Anathema, requires an actual reduction (from not-zero to zero) - simply being in combat on zero does not trigger such text.

Hmm. Segregation by location vs global event. Methinks the latter better helps the community. At any rate, nothing else happened, so we might as well be having only one this year.

Also, it is not quite so simple as "ask and it shall be given". In my end of the woods, getting people to fly in for one weekend of V:tES is possibly doable once a year. Getting them to fly in for one week plus the weekend once a year, not so much. Additionally, 3 countries with a total of 4 regions means that doing a separate storyline event is a little pointless.

Given the current state of the game, making players feel like they are a part of a global whole instead of giving the impression that we are each on our own seems like a better move.

Extending the deadline shows that VEKN cares about the players, especially since there were requests to that effect.

Messages.Author: ICL
Messages.Body:
I'm assuming that the mention of extending to October 31st is in effect.

How flexible are the rules?

Until we went to play, I thought there were multiple adversaries in play at a time. After playing, only one being in play seems suboptimal to me. We never got to the auction for the All High as the effort to kill Loki with the decks at the table was too much in combination with how nuking the adversaries really didn't do much, so there wasn't enough incentive to gangbang the adversaries. I thought there was going to be two in play at a time, which means that there should be an easy kill all of the time for decks that are into that sort of thing.

The magic weapons are too weak. Now, whether making them melee weapons helps or hurts or doesn't matter at all isn't entirely clear, but I'd look to try to upvalue them.

The question about multirushing adversaries is important. We ruled that you couldn't as the action is "enter combat with a revealed adversary" or whatever, not enter combat with adversary XYZ. As FBI Special Affairs has the magic word ally on it, does that mean it gets ignored for adversaries?

For Jormungandr and Sutr, the way they read, if you have one free location/equipment, you can just choose that one and never be affected. I would change their abilities to something like burn all locations/equipment or pay 2 pool for each one you want to retain.

Traveller Card Game

Messages.Author: AaronC
Messages.Body:
> In each player's minion phase, any minion controlled by that player may take an undirected action to enter combat with the revealed Adversary. If its life is reduced to zero by combat damage it is burned and removed from the game.
>
My understanding of the NRA is that this is a repeatable action since the power to do it comes from the "rulebook" and not from a card in hand or in play and it is not a bleed action or vote action.

I do not think that the word "an" as in "an action" means "(exactly) one". Normally "one" means "exactly one" and "a/an" means "one or more".

I think that all your minions can do it: I do not think that the "any" of "any minion" means "one and only one". I think it means "up to all".

Of course, this is just my feeble logic probing the murky depths that is the English language.

Messages.Author: Miasmat
Messages.Body:
I like ICL's idea of having multiple adversaries out at a time. This means I get to attack the one I can be effective against, rather than waiting for the 1 deck on the table who can do <insert quirky combat trick to get around the adversary's power>.

I'm partial to something like:
On turn 3 (and the next X turns), open an adversary slot.
Whenever there's an open adversary slot, reveal an adversary and its reward.
You can attack any adversary, and if you burn it with combat damage, you get its reward. Replace that adversary immediately.
You can tune X, but I'm partial to something like 3 or 4. ICL wanted X=2. Currently, it's X=1.

The bigger X is, the more of the Adversaries' "bad stuff" you'll have to face at once. But you get more choices for combat that you can actually be effective in.

Food for thought.

And I'd like to echo the sentiment that the rewards are generally weak. The only ones that I think are worthwhile is the free untap (Gjallahorn), +1 intercept/stealth (Sleipnir), +1 intercept & environmental damage (Huginn), hunting ground + environmental damage (Geri).

The big problem with the rewards is that you can't count on which ones you'll get, or that you'll get them early enough to matter. So, you have to build your deck to be able to function without them. Which means, they probably don't matter much.

Most of the rewards don't much help further your goal of ousting your prey. And you already wasted at least 1 action killing the Adversary for it. You could be plenty successful with a normal deck and totally ignore the Adversaries.

On the other hand, the storyline-only werewolves are great. I really liked having a wide selection of them (made cheaper with Caern + Charisma + other tricks). The werewolf-only cards are great. I think this is a nice way to add non-vampires to the game, instead of stupid Imbued stupidness.
